chunks: From him, from al-Sindi ibn al-Rabi', from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, at what age do the legal rulings apply to children?' He said, 'At thirteen and fourteen years.' I said, 'And if he does not experience wet dreams during that time?' He said, 'And even if he does not experience wet dreams, the legal rulings still apply to him.'

key_terms.يَحْتَلِمْ: to experience wet dreams (sign of puberty)

ai.seo_question: At what age do Islamic legal rulings apply to children if they have not yet experienced wet dreams?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the ages of thirteen and fourteen serve as the definitive markers for legal responsibility (bulugh) in boys, a ruling derived from the consensus of the Imams. Notably, the hadith clarifies that the physical sign of seminal emission is not a prerequisite for accountability; rather, the passage of this specific age range is sufficient to trigger the application of Shariah rulings, emphasizing the objective nature of maturity in Shia jurisprudence. This principle underscores the transition from childhood to adulthood based on chronological age rather than solely on physiological development.
